Issue 11, a test-only fix made first (no plan cycle — the arbiter's rule for small already-made fixes), at 638558e. gate: see entry @ 638558e. Doc: docs/phases/wait-child-test-waits-for-its-child.md.

Background: the 3.14.7 release-tree suite failed once — 1 failed / 2,274 passed, tests/test_watcher_lock.py::test_wait_child_terminates_and_reports_a_child_still_running, 1-minute load average ~48 — and passed (2,275) on an immediate rerun; the release went out on the rerun. I did NOT capture the failure message (I had tailed the run to two lines), so what follows is a demonstrated mechanism, not a proven cause.

Established by replaying the test's steps outside pytest: the test gives a spawned 'python -c print(...); sleep' 0.5 s, lets _wait_child terminate it, and asserts the text is in the dump. A child that has not printed when SIGTERM lands leaves an empty dump: 0.5 s budget on a calm machine → text 15/15; a 5 ms budget (a starved child) → empty 15/15. Ruled out: os.killpg racing the child's setsid (0/30 — Popen returns after exec). Not explained: two of five solo runs of the OLD test took ~5 s instead of ~0.6 s; no slow step in 30 timed replays of the test's own flow.

Change: tests/test_watcher_lock.py, that one test — the child creates a marker file in tmp_path AFTER its flushed print; the test waits for it (_wait(ready.exists, timeout=60)) and only then starts the 0.5 s clock. Assertions unchanged. No product code, and _wait_child/_child_output untouched. The other two helper tests do not have this race (one waits for the child's exit first; the other reads its line first and asserts nothing about output text).

Worth your eye: my first attempt read the child's first line from the pipe, as the sibling test does. It failed deterministically with 'output: <none>' — the buffered reader swallows the rest of the pipe, which is the very text _child_output must find through communicate(). Hence a readiness signal that does not touch the pipe.

Verified: the helper tests, 4 passed × 6 consecutive runs. Against a slow-starting child (sleep(2) before its print — starvation made deterministic): old flow → text captured 0/3, new flow → 3/3. Not verified: that the flake is gone under real load ~48 — not reproducible on demand (12/12 passes of the old test under eight busy CPU loops, load ~10).

GATE: PASS | scope skipped | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2275 passed, 5 skipped, 7m52s)
checked: HEAD 638558e
not checked — scope: no implementation boundary recorded (plan approved before 3.2.0, or a legacy cycle) — scope not enforced

Approved 638558e. The marker establishes that the child has flushed its expected output before the 0.5-second timeout under test begins, without consuming the pipe that _child_output must inspect. Timeout/output/termination assertions remain intact, startup waiting is bounded, and finally still reaps the child if readiness or later assertions fail. No product code or helper behavior changed.

Verification: reviewer focused helper tests: 4 passed, 16 deselected. git diff --check HEAD^..HEAD clean. Gate PASS at 638558e: 2275 passed, 5 skipped, accepted without rerun. The gate skipped scope enforcement because no plan boundary exists; reviewed the complete commit manually: one test plus its phase/roadmap/issue documentation, consistent with the disclosed direct-impl small-fix scope.

The documentation appropriately distinguishes the demonstrated race from the unproven cause of the uncaptured release failure. Minor wording note for closeout: the new source comment says the starved release child 'was terminated before it had printed'; keep that phrased as a possible mechanism, consistent with the phase document, rather than treating the historical cause as established. This does not block the test fix. No outstanding code findings or interjections.
